text:
incident_bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Service=streaming-pipeline latency p99 > 2.5s (SLO breach). Auto-paging @oncall. Incident ID: INC-2026-1872

pagerduty: Paging jamie_oncall (primary).

jamie_oncall: on it. grabbing dashboards now. any initial customer-facing impact?

tara_sre: +1 seeing p95 jump to ~600ms, p99 ~2.8s for streaming-v2 in us-west-2. Errors are low (5xx ~0.1%) but there are lots of streaming stalls where clients wait for tokens.

mike_runtime: logs show a spike in cache miss rate on prefix-cache for the new prefix-hash rollout. miss-rate went from ~7% -> ~48% starting 1869994200.

jamie_oncall: oof. did rollout finish recently? who merged the prefix-hash change?

aaron_eng: that was my canary deploy 1869994100. small rollout to 10% to validate ordering change in prefix hashing. I saw no failures in canary but maybe traffic patterns differ.

tara_sre: can confirm miss-rate correlates with canary start. KV eviction counters also spiked. looks like new hash function moved keys to different shards, invalidating warm cache.

jamie_oncall: impact: streaming path uses prefix cache heavily for short prompts. high miss-rate -> more backend decoding -> higher tail latency and streaming stalls. need quick mitigation to restore hit rate.

mike_runtime: mitigation options: 1) rollback the prefix-hash change (fast) 2) temporarily increase cache size / TTL to warm > takes time 3) route traffic away from canary nodes (if we can identify) 4) enable hot-warm replication for prefix cache (manual, takes ~20m).

aaron_eng: I can revert the hash change right now and trigger a rollout to fix canary. revert commit: `git revert 0f3a9b2c` and push.

jamie_oncall: do it. prefer rollback to avoid prolonged customer impact. keep me posted when revert is in canary and then prod.

aaron_eng: starting revert now. running deploy job.

incident_bot: deploy-bot: Starting rollout of revert commit to canary (10%): job_id=deploy-1872-canary.

mike_runtime: while that is running, I'll add temporary traffic split: move 80% away from canary nodes. patching routing policy.

tara_sre: +1 apply. We should also pre-warm cache if we can: run a cache-warm job that replays hot prefixes from logs to populate new hash buckets once revert lands.

jamie_oncall: mike, how long to change routing?

mike_runtime: +5m. doing now.

mike_runtime: routing patch applied. canary traffic reduced to 2%. monitoring hit-rate.

tara_sre: current metrics after route change: p95 down to 420ms, p99 down to 1.1s from 2.8s. miss-rate dropped to ~22% (was 48%). stalls reduced but still some tail.

aaron_eng: revert finished in canary, starting rollout to 50%. job_id=deploy-1872-roll50.

incident_bot: deploy-bot: rollout to 50% successful. next step: 100% in 5m if metrics stable.

jamie_oncall: good. tara, any downstream systems impacted? billing, dedupe, etc?

tara_sre: no change to error rates. embedding pipeline unaffected. Only streaming-v2 prefix-cache path. no evidence of cross-service corruption.

mike_runtime: quick check of KV stats (from a node):
```
kv_prefix_cache: hits=120k misses=35k miss_rate=22% evictions=4.1k
kv_shard_distribution: shard_0=31% shard_1=28% shard_2=41%
```

jamie_oncall: thanks. set a post-rollback watch for 30m. if p99 stays <1s and miss-rate <10% we'll close.

aaron_eng: rolling to 100% now. deploy-bot job_id=deploy-1872-roll100.

incident_bot: deploy-bot: rollout to 100% successful.

tara_sre: metrics: p95=180ms, p99=650ms, miss_rate=9%. streaming stalls are gone in latest 5m window.

mike_runtime: started cache-warm replay for safety. replayed top-10k prefixes, warming new buckets.

jamie_oncall: Customer impact summary: brief SLO breach for streaming-v2 starting 1869994200 -> 1869994520 (~5.5m visible impact window). Estimated affected requests ~120k, small fraction of customers experienced token stalls or slower streaming. No elevated 5xx rate or data loss.

tara_sre: proposed actions postmortem: - revert caused immediate fix; need to update rollout playbook for hashing changes - add automated pre-warm when changing hash function - add canary traffic routing to isolate cache warm state - add regression test for prefix distribution skew.

aaron_eng: ack. I'll write up PR with safer rollout steps and pre-warm job.

jamie_oncall: handing off to tara_sre for post-incident follow-up. I’m stepping off oncall in 20m; leave any ongoing checklist here.

tara_sre: taking handoff. I'll collect logs and draft incident report. assigning follow-ups: @aaron_eng (rollout playbook + PR), @mike_runtime (routing automation + prewarm job), @jamie_oncall (verify postmortem draft).

mike_runtime: noted. I'll also add an alert for prefix-cache miss-rate > 15% in prod (currently 9%).

incident_bot: Incident INC-2026-1872: mitigation complete. Status: mitigated -> monitoring.

jamie_oncall: :white_check_mark: great work team. closing active paging. will re-open if regressions observed.

tara_sre: closing thread once postmortem posted. thanks everyone. :coffee:
